description: Adversarial-counsel detection mechanism per PRD §6.7 and §7.10. This is a v1 requirement — the single highest-UPL-risk moment in the product. Uses explicit branching questions, NOT natural-language analysis of uploaded letters (NL-detection deferred beyond v1).

questions.question: Has the other party or anyone representing them contacted you since you sent the letter?
Did they mention a lawyer, an attorney, or legal action?
Did they threaten to sue you, file a countersuit, or take you to court?

trigger_response.heading: This Situation Has Moved Beyond Writing Assistance
trigger_response.body: Based on what you've described, the other party has involved legal representation or threatened legal action. At this point, the situation involves legal strategy and judgment that goes beyond what a writing tool can responsibly help with.
trigger_response.reassurance: This is actually common in disputes like yours — it often means the other party is taking your claim seriously. People in this situation typically consult with a licensed attorney to understand their options.
action_items: Do not respond to the attorney or legal threat without consulting your own legal representation.
Keep all documents and correspondence you've received — they may be important.
The letter and materials you've already generated are yours to share with any attorney you consult.

notes: The question-based mechanism is chosen deliberately over NL-detection because for the single highest-UPL-risk moment the reliable mechanism beats the elegant one. NL-detection of uploaded adversarial letters is explicitly deferred beyond v1 per PRD §7.10.
